rationale:
Issue #1223 (body embedded in source_candidate.issue_check.linked_issues) reports that with respectsExistingLineBreaks:false the break after #endif is collapsed, emitting non-parsing Swift (`#endif struct S {}`) when an #if wraps an attribute of the following decl. The minimized production patch touches only Sources/SwiftFormat/PrettyPrint/TokenStreamCreator.swift and only the newline behavior of breaks around #endif: hunk 1 selects .elective/.soft NewlineBehavior for the break after node.poundEndif by context, hunk 3 emits a .hard break when an attribute list ends with an IfConfigDeclSyntax (the exact issue scenario), and hunk 4 makes the postfix-#if clause breaks .soft and drops the now-redundant after(poundEndif) break superseded by hunk 1. All three are the same root cause (elective breaks after #endif being discarded), with no formatting, refactor, doc, config, or feature change; automatic minimization removed hunk 2 and post_minimization_validation is PASS, so the retained subset is the validated minimum. The trigger is the unchanged upstream test from the same fixing commit; its first case is verbatim the issue reproducer, and it uses only pre-existing helpers (assertPrettyPrintEqual, the file's private configuration(respectingExistingLineBreaks:)) and no API introduced by the fix (NewlineBehavior, .break(_:size:newlines:), isNestedInPostfixIfConfig, config.respectsExistingLineBreaks all pre-exist, as none are added by the diff). Strict evidence for both the original and post-minimization states passes every gate: build on both revisions, unique selector, buggy differential reproducing only testIfConfigKeepsRequiredLineBreakAfterEndif, deterministic across 3 repetitions, fixed isolated/suite/reversed clean, and fixed full suite all green. active_same_project_root_causes is empty, so #1223 is not a duplicate.

Issue #1223 reports that with respectsExistingLineBreaks: false, the required line break after #endif is collapsed so a declaration is glued onto the #endif line, producing unparseable Swift (`#endif struct S {}`). The fix commit 4f78786 (PR #1225, 'Fix #endif gluing onto the following token', message 'fix ##1223') changes exactly the break/newline behavior around #endif in Sources/SwiftFormat/PrettyPrint/TokenStreamCreator.swift, and the trigger test testIfConfigKeepsRequiredLineBreakAfterEndif embeds the issue's exact reproducer (#if FLAG / @frozen / #endif / struct S {}) with respectingExistingLineBreaks: false, asserting the break after #endif is preserved. Same defect across issue, trigger, and fix. The minimized production patch keeps three hunks, all in the single production file and all on the #endif line-break path: (1) context-sensitive NewlineBehavior for the break after node.poundEndif, (3) a hard break when an attribute list ends with an IfConfigDecl, and (4) soft newlines on postfix-#if clause breaks plus removal of the now-duplicated after(poundEndif) break that hunk 1 subsumes. Automatic minimization reports chosen_subset == minimal_hunks == [1,3,4] with the fourth hunk removed and post_minimization_validation PASS, so every retained hunk is behaviorally required by the trigger; there is no formatting-only, doc-only, config-only, or feature change. The trigger is the unmodified upstream test portion of the same fixing commit (removed_external_dependency: false) and relies only on pre-existing test infrastructure (PrettyPrintTestCase.assertPrettyPrintEqual, the file's existing private configuration(respectingExistingLineBreaks:) helper) and pre-existing production API (NewlineBehavior, .break(.same, size:newlines:), config.respectsExistingLineBreaks); no API introduced by the fix is used. Machine-generated strict evidence passes all gates both originally and post-minimization: build.both_versions, selectors.present_and_unique (1 unique selector), trigger.buggy_differential with the declared selector reproducing, trigger.deterministic (3 fingerprint groups over 3 repetitions), trigger.fixed_clean, full_suite.buggy_reproduces_only_triggers, and full_suite.fixed_all_green, with no failed checks. active_same_project_root_causes is empty, so swiftlang/swift-format#1223 is not a duplicate, and it matches the single allowed verified issue key.
